newsitem.title: UK: Sears says to press on with Freemans sale.
newsitem.headline: Sears says to press on with Freemans sale.

text.p: British retailer Sears plc on Tuesday reaffirmed its commitment to selling its Freemans plc catalogue shopping business to the privately-owned Littlewoods Organisation, despite a monopolies and mergers investigation into the proposed deal.

In a statement, Sears said that although the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) review meant the contract for the sale first signed on January 12 would now lapse, "Sears remains committed to a the disposal of Freemans and intends to work with Littlewoods and cooperate fully with the MMC in its investigation".

Sears' chief executive Liam Strong commented, "We continue to believe that this proposed consolidation would result in benefits for Freemans, for its mail order customers and for Sears' shareholders."
The deal had been priced at 395 million stg, and retail analysts had described the government decision to start a monopolies enquiry as surprising.
